events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Ketchikan Gateway Borough
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Heavy rain has fallen in and around Ketchikan through this afternoon
and will continue into tonight. An additional 1 to 2.5 inches is
expected by daybreak Friday. Reports of flooding and minor slides
have been observed. Ketchikan Creek is at bankfull and could climb
into minor flood stage tonight.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...In and around Ketchikan.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas, as
well as area streams and rivers. Water over roadways. Possible
isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 808 PM AKDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in and
around Ketchikan. Many area streams and rivers are near or at
bankfull and could climb into minor flooding tonight. Minor
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Between 2.5 and
4 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to
2.5 inches are possible by daybreak Friday.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ketchikan, Saxman and Ward Cove.

- For Carlanna Lake Dam in Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 522.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 524.0 feet.


For Fawn Lake in Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 326.0 feet.


For Ketchikan Lake:
At 5:00pm the stage was 337.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 349.0 feet.

Impacts:
At 348.0 feet: There will be 1 foot of water going over the emergency
spillway at the dam with bankful conditions along Ketchikan Creek.
At 349.0 feet: There will be 2 feet of water going over the emergency
spillway. Minor flooding will occur along Ketchikan Creek mainly
below the Park Ave bridge. There are some tidal effects along Creek
St and flooding could be worse at high tides.

For Ketchikan Powerhouse:
At 5:00pm the stage was 62.2 feet.
Flood Stage is 63.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 63.5 feet: Minor flooding will occur along Ketchikan Creek mainly
below the Park Ave bridge. There are some tidal effects along Creek
St and flooding could be worse at high tides.


For Lake Connell Dam:
At 1:00pm the stage was 250.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 252.0 feet.

Impacts:
At 251.0 feet: Water will begin to approach low lying areas of trails
and picnic areas around Ward Lake.

For Leask Creek at Shelter Cove:
At 5:30pm the stage was 22.2 feet.


For Whitman Lake Dam near Ketchikan:
At 5:00pm the stage was 373.6 feet.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Glacier Bay; Eastern Chichagof Island; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Through Friday morning, a series of fronts will bring multiple
rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall across the Alaska Panhandle.
The second round of heavy rain is expected to bring an additional
0.5 to 1.5 inches tonight into Friday morning, with the higher end
QPF amounts expected for Baranof and Admiralty Islands. More
localized lower or higher amounts are possible due to terrain
effects.

Even higher rain amounts are possible for parts of the central
panhandle associated with the front tonight as its low develops
inland and moves northward, though there is still a lack of
confidence on the exact location of these higher rates. As of now,
the highest amounts are expected to move into southern Baranof
Island up into Stephens Passage, though some elevated rainfall
amounts may still reach Sitka and other parts of the central and
northern panhandle.

While these forecasted rain amounts are expected to bring rises to
small creeks and rivers in the area, there is no flooding
anticipated at this time.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to monitor the
situation and update our forecast.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Zapata; Jim Hogg; Brooks; Inland Kenedy; Starr; Southern Hidalgo; Inland Willacy; Inland Cameron; Northern Hidalgo
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...STRONG NORTHERLY WINDS FRIDAY NIGHT INCREASE WILDFIRE THREAT...

.A strong front pushes south through Deep South Texas and the Rio
Grande Valley on Friday, with a secondary surge of strong
northerly winds arriving late Friday evening into late Saturday
morning. Relative humidity values are expected to drop Friday
afternoon with little to no recovery into Saturday morning. Any
wildfire that can develop will behave dangerously with erratic
growth and spread due to strong winds and lower humidity. A Red
Flag Warning is in effect.

The National Weather Service in Brownsville has issued a Red Flag
Warning for Red Flag Warning, which is in effect from 1 PM Friday
to 7 AM CDT Saturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in
effect.

* WINDS...Northerly 15-25 mph, gusting as high as 35-55 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 25 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that can develop will behave dangerously with
erratic growth and spread.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook has been replaced by the Flood Watch, out for
Guam, Rota, Tinian and Saipan.

Residents on these islands need to closely monitor this developing
situation as flood watches, advisories and flash flood warnings could
be issued later.

If living near streams and rivers, prepare to move items away from
stream and river banks. Make sure storm drains nearby are not
clogged, especially If living at low-lying areas.
